column2: TruncateBytes truncates s to at most max bytes, preserving valid UTF-8 and whole characters.
Why character boundaries matter: WeCom group bot markdown has a hard 4096 **byte** limit, not
a character limit; Chinese characters take 3 bytes. Direct byte slicing can split a character and produce invalid
UTF-8, causing rejection or garbled squares. Starting at the budget position,
backtrack to the nearest rune start (utf8.RuneStart identifies continuation bytes 0b10xxxxxx).
max<=0 means unlimited. Append an ellipsis after truncation unless max cannot fit it.
If max is shorter than the ellipsis, omit it and truncate directly to avoid exceeding max.
OneLine compresses multiline text to a single line: collapse all whitespace, then truncate by character count.
Used for IM title lines; summaries often contain newlines that would disrupt tables or titles.
max<=0 means no length limit.
TruncateRunes truncates s to at most max characters, not bytes, appending an ellipsis when exceeded.
max<=0 means unlimited.
Unlike TruncateBytes, this follows platform character limits: WeCom counts bytes, Telegram counts characters.
Using the wrong unit causes no error, only unexpectedly short messages (one Chinese character takes 3 bytes;
a 4096-byte cut retains about 1365 characters), so retain both functions and select by channel.
TruncateHTML truncates an HTML fragment by character count without leaving partial tags.
Direct character truncation can produce a partial tag such as `<a href="htt`; the platform parser may
reject the whole message or swallow following text as an attribute. First truncate by characters,
then check for an unclosed trailing `<` and backtrack before it.
Do not balance tags (such as adding ): Telegram's HTML parser closes open tags automatically;
implementing balancing would require handling quoted attributes, comments, and self-closing tags for little benefit.
If the tail starts with a partial `<` (no `>` after the last `<`), backtrack before it.
Likewise, backtrack before a partial HTML entity (such as `&` cut to `&amp`).
An entity-only parser may reject the **entire message** for a partial entity. Oversized
batch messages are common and should not cause the whole notification to be lost.
packItemCount calculates how many **whole** items fit the budget for batch-message packing.
Why pack whole items instead of rendering everything then truncating: truncation makes later entries disappear,
while delivery records still mark them delivered. Neither the message nor history reveals the loss,
so vulnerabilities silently vanish. Whole-item packing keeps excluded entries in the database for the next batch;
kept tells the caller how many items this message actually delivered.
Parameters: maxSize<=0 means unlimited; reserve allows for message headers and footers;
size supplies platform-specific measurement (WeCom/DingTalk count bytes, Telegram counts characters;
using the wrong unit silently compresses Chinese messages far below the limit);
render produces the actual text of item idx, whose content-dependent length cannot be estimated.
Return at least 1 when items remain. Even an extremely long single item must be sent, relying on the caller's
final truncation, or it could block the entire batch forever.
byteSize / runeSize name packItemCount's measurement units, avoiding anonymous
func(s string) int closures that obscure which unit the call uses.
assetLine renders assets as one display line, omitting those beyond limit and showing the total count.
One vulnerability may anchor dozens of assets; listing all would overflow the message.
itoa is a short alias for strconv.Itoa, used only in display text to avoid importing strconv everywhere.
telegramTextLimit is the Telegram sendMessage text-field limit, in characters.
telegramChannel implements the Telegram Bot API.
Platform characteristics:
- Authentication is entirely in the URL path (/bot<token>/sendMessage); no signing needed.
- Use HTML parse mode rather than MarkdownV2: MarkdownV2 requires escaping `_*[]()~`>#+-=|{}.!`
(18 characters); missing one rejects the whole message. HTML needs only & < > escaped.
- Business errors also appear in HTTP 200 responses; inspect ok.
Telegram allows about 1 message/second in private chats and 20/minute in groups. Use a conservative value.
Bot Token is the complete credential; chat_id is only a recipient, not a secret (without a Token it cannot send messages).
base_url determines which API endpoint receives the Token (such as a self-hosted reverse proxy); changing it requires explicit Token input.
429 is rate limiting and can be retried after backoff; others (400 invalid parameters, 401 invalid token, 403 blocked,
404 missing chat) are configuration errors that retries cannot repair.
telegramEndpoint constructs the sendMessage URL. Empty base_url uses the official API;
nonempty supports self-hosted Bot API reverse proxies, common on domestic networks.
Do not pass err through: the URL contains the Bot Token, and even addr must not be echoed here.
telegramHTML renders the HTML body and returns it with the number of entries actually included (see Channel.Send).
Telegram limits **characters**, so packing also measures characters (runeSize).
telegramReservedRunes reserves characters for the message title and possible truncation notice.
telegramBatchLine renders one batch entry, unescaped; the caller escapes it consistently.
telegramBatchTitle renders the batch title line. Count entries **actually included in this message**,
not the batch total, or readers will assume the header number covers everything.
telegramEscape escapes HTML text content.
Telegram recognizes only these three entities. Existing entities such as & are escaped again, deliberately:
we want to display original characters, not allow HTML injection.
telegramEscapeAttr escapes HTML attribute values, handling quotes in addition to text escaping:
quotes in URLs could prematurely close href and turn subsequent content into an injection point.
webhookChannel is a generic Webhook adapter with user-defined URL, method, headers, and JSON template.
It avoids separate implementations for Slack / Mattermost / Discord / self-hosted systems;
one configurable template can cover all of them.
Generic Webhooks have no official limit; return 0 for unlimited by default, leaving users to match peer capacity.
Mask url and headers: destinations often contain tokens and custom headers usually contain credentials;
both appear in API responses and must be protected.
Editing one header consequently requires resubmitting all headers (masked values mean keep unchanged).
This tradeoff is deliberate: prefer re-entry over exposing credentials to the browser.
The destination is url. Changing url requires explicit headers input, or the original Authorization header
would be sent unchanged to the new destination, the primary masking-bypass path.
webhookDefaultTemplate is the fallback request body when no template is provided: straightforward JSON
covering most self-hosted receivers that store incoming JSON.
webhookTemplateData is the context exposed to user templates.
SentAt is this delivery's timestamp (RFC3339), for receiver records.
StatusLabel describes a status transition, such as pending -> fixed; empty for other events.
GET has no body. Adding content to query parameters exceeds template capabilities and conflicts with GET semantics,
so GET suits only receivers triggered by an endpoint hit.
The template renders JSON text; convert it to json.RawMessage and send unchanged,
avoiding double escaping that would wrap the intended structure in a JSON string.
Allow overrides, but apply after headers so explicit configuration takes precedence.
Generic Webhooks do not truncate bodies (the receiver is user-controlled and body_template determines size),
so the entire batch counts as delivered.
renderWebhookBody renders the request body using the user template or default template.
parseWebhookTemplate parses the template.
missingkey=zero renders absent map keys as zero values rather than errors. This context is a struct;
its main purpose is to avoid range errors when .Items is empty. The actual concern is nil .Items.
webhookTemplateFuncs supplies helper functions exposed to templates.
json serializes any value as JSON.
This function is essential, not cosmetic: without it users can only interpolate {{.Title}} directly;
a quote or newline in a vulnerability title then makes the entire request invalid JSON. The receiver
rejects it with a JSON parse error, offering no obvious clue that a title quote caused the problem.
jsons embeds a JSON fragment inside another JSON string value, applying one layer of string escaping.
Remove outer quotes; callers decide whether to add them.
weComMarkdownLimit is the WeCom group bot markdown content hard limit in bytes, not characters.
It is the strictest limit among all six channels and the primary reason for TruncateBytes.
weComChannel implements WeCom group bots.
Platform characteristics:
- Authentication uses only the URL key; signing is unsupported, so the webhook URL is the entire credential.
- markdown content is limited to 4096 **bytes**; oversized messages are rejected, not truncated. Chinese uses 3 bytes per character,
leaving room for only a little over a thousand characters; client-side truncation is required.
- Rate limit is 20 messages/minute, also enforced client-side.
WeCom has only one credential: the Webhook URL key. Signing is unsupported;
the entire URL is the credential and no other fields need masking.
WeCom's sole Webhook field is both destination and credential, so no old credential remains after changing the URL.
Batch messages can be long (50 one-line items plus prefix), easily exceeding 4096 bytes.
Truncate here rather than relying on platform rejection: rejection loses the whole batch, while truncation delivers some entries.
45009 means the API limit was exceeded. The platform's rate window rolls, so retry after backoff can work;
classify it explicitly as retryable. Reaching this means client rate_per_min is too aggressive;
retrying is only a fallback. The real fix is lowering this channel's rate limit.
93000 means an invalid webhook key: permanent failure, not repairable by retry.
